stories.title: Northern Cyprus ferry disaster: at least seven dead as vessel capsizes – latest updates
stories.summary: At least seven people have died after a ferry carrying nearly 270 passengers and crew capsized off the coast of Turkish-occupied northern Cyprus, local media reported. An estimated 237 people have been rescued, Northern Cyprus’ prime minister, Ünal Üstel, told the TRT news channel, adding that the ferry had faced adverse weather conditions and began taking in water just 15 minutes after departure. Local media report that an intensive search and rescue effort was launched after the boat capsized off the coastal town of Kyrenia earlier today. The ferry had been travelling to the Turkish port of Tasucu. I have just spoken to Mehmet Harmanci, who as mayor of breakaway northern Nicosia, says he is overseeing efforts to gather warm clothes and other essentials for the wounded. “There are 23 still missing and others who have also been injured although we don’t know to what degree,” he told the Guardian. “The wounded are being sent to hospital here in (northern) Nicosia and we are gathering warm clothes for them.” Harmanci described the disaster as the worst ever witnessed in the 43 years since the territory declared independence. “We have not seen anything like this before. It’s very serious,” he said. Four Turkish Cypriot coast guard vessels and a civilian passenger boat have been deployed to the scene, along with five Turkish coastguard vessels and two helicopters, the Turkish Cypriot interior ministry said in a statement. The prime minister of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Ünal Üstel, has posted an update on X about the “tragic shipwreck”.
